record.title: Keep consumer operations in consumer repositories
record.intent: Align the public taskctl backlog with ownership of the general-purpose protocol and tooling.
requirements: Own tasking state, contributor/onboarding documentation, and a bounded audit of this scope change. Consumer operational work and full migration artifacts belong in consumer repositories.
Preserve all prior task identities, contracts and receipts. Use explicit CAS revisions; do not claim that deferred consumer migrations occurred.
Keep the existing dependency gates for the protocol checkpoint, remote kernel and native-v1 assessment. General compatibility evidence remains required.
acceptance: Remaining open consumer migration contracts become explicit general-purpose compatibility/conformance tasks, with unchanged prerequisite edges and open lifecycle.
Historical Brule tracking closes with observed consumer evidence; Brule owns its converter, source archive, integration proof and migration receipt.
Doctor, currency, frontier, history and immutable-evidence checks pass; no protocol/runtime/source-distribution changes or consumer migrations are implied.

review.rationale: Reviewed the still-open work definition and prerequisite observations after explicit consumer-ownership rescoping. Existing prerequisite edges are unchanged. This review acknowledges the plan, not implementation, migration, conformance completion, checkpoint approval or protocol freeze.

evidence.ownership: docs/CONSUMER-OWNERSHIP.md and docs/proof/consumer-ownership/revisions.json: scope/causal-order review only; this task remains open and its acceptance work is not claimed complete.
evidence.validation: docs/CONSUMER-OWNERSHIP.md and docs/proof/consumer-ownership/revisions.json: scope/causal-order review only; this task remains open and its acceptance work is not claimed complete.
